cover: Backups vs disaster recovery: you need both

slides.title: A backup is a copy of your data
slides.body: It tells you a copy exists. It doesn't tell you how to use it, how long that takes, or who does it.

slides.title: Recovery is the plan to run again
slides.body: Hosting, settings, secrets, integrations and the steps to bring them back, written down and rehearsed.

slides.title: How much work can you lose?
slides.body: That's your recovery point objective. Back up nightly and a 4pm failure can cost a day of orders.

slides.title: How long can you be down?
slides.body: That's your recovery time objective. Lower numbers cost more, so choose them on purpose.

slides.title: Restore it, or it's a guess
slides.body: A backup nobody has restored may not work. A timed restore test also gives you your real recovery time.
